questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend starting with three AI projects rather than ten?
options: Each needs an owner, setup and new habits, and three is what a small team can carry
Most AI tools limit how many separate projects a single account can run at once
With ten projects running, it becomes impossible to measure any of the baselines
Three projects is the minimum a business needs to justify buying a new AI tool
questions.explain: The lesson says each project needs an owner, a little setup, testing and a change in someone's habits, and three in parallel is about as much as a small business can carry while still running day to day.

questions.q: A four-person marketing agency has chosen meeting summaries as its quick win and weekly client reports as its core workflow. Which third project best completes the balanced portfolio?
options: Writing SOPs for the office's internal onboarding checklist
A fully automated chatbot that answers client questions alone
Reactivating past clients with a consistent check-in campaign
Summarizing the transcripts of internal team meetings
questions.explain: The third slot is a growth bet tied to revenue, and the lesson gives reactivating past customers as an example; a fully automated customer-facing chatbot is listed as a first-project trap.

questions.q: Two weeks into an AI pilot for drafting quotes, a pet-grooming business owner feels it's saving time but can't show by how much. Which first-project trap from the lesson did she fall into?
questions.explain: The lesson warns that if you don't measure 'before,' you can't prove 'after,' which is why every project needs a baseline measured before anything changes.
